blocks.html: Dani’el saw in his vision that the initial horn of the male goat was shattered, resulting in the emergence of four horns. Historical-critical scholars commonly identify the "little horn" as Antiochus IV Epiphanes, who was replaced by one of four horns after his reign, according to some interpretations. The text in Dani’el 8:10-14 pertains to the actions of Antiochus towards the Jewish population during his reign, a period that culminated with the Maccabean Revolt and the rededication of The Altar. Furthermore, it is believed that Dani’el 11, which mentions Persia and Greece and two rulers, pertains to the Seleucids dynasty and more specifically to Antiochus Epiphanes, who is identified as "The King of the North."

blocks.html: Not long after this the king [Antiochus IV] sent an Athenian senator to force the Jews to abandon the customs of their ancestors and live no longer by the laws of יהוה; also to profane the temple in Yerushalayim and dedicate it to Olympian Zeus, and that on Mount Gerizim to Zeus the Hospitable, as the inhabitants of the place requested...They also brought into the temple things that were forbidden, so that the altar was covered with [the blood] abominable offerings prohibited by the laws [a pig]. A man could not keep the Shabbat or celebrate the traditional feasts [of יהוה], nor even admit that he was a Jew. At the suggestion of the citizens of Ptolemais, a decree was issued ordering the neighbouring Greek cities to act in the same way against the Jews: oblige them to partake of the sacrifices and put to death those who would not consent to adopt the customs of the Greeks. It was obvious, therefore, that disaster impended.

blocks.html: As Antiochus was engaged in his endeavors in Egypt, a rumor started circulating that he had passed away. Jason, who had been removed from his position as High Priest, enlisted 1,000 soldiers and launched an unexpected assault on the city of Yerushalayim. While a commotion occurred in Yerushalayim, Menelaus, the High Priest designated by Antiochus, was compelled to escape the city. In 167 BC, the King, who was furious after being defeated in Egypt, launched an attack on Yerushalayim, brought back Menelaus, and proceeded to execute a considerable number of Jewish people.

Thus, the passage reads as follows:
Tas’loniqim Bet/2 Thessalonians 2

blocks.html: 3 Let no one deceive you in any way, because the falling away is to come first [rebellion against The Torah/Law or Transgression of Desolation], and the man of lawlessness [or image of a man in whom The Law is abolished] is to be revealed [to be The False Messiah 666- xςς Jesus], the son of Desolation, [See Dan_11:36-39] 4 he [666- xςς Jesus] who opposes and exalts himself [in the hearts/minds of man] above all that is called Elohim or that is worshipped, so that he sits as Elohim in the Dwelling Place [the body of man] of Elohim, showing himself that he is Elohim
